assumptions: x-forwarded-for is the client key available in middleware via $request.headers
error_type accessdenied is acceptable for a 429-style rejection
the group-level middleware attachment is the intended way new endpoints inherit the limiter
confusions: The skill/catalogue never shows XanoScript syntax for attaching middleware to an api_group; six variants were refused by the parser with unclear messages ('Invalid block: name', 'Invalid kind for middleware - static:text[]', 'Expecting static:object[]'), so the error shape is inconsistent.

The skill names a middleware file path only indirectly; no example middleware file or the middleware block grammar (exception_policy, input/stack keys) is shown, so I inferred it from the pull layout.
Whether $request.headers is the correct way to read the client address in middleware is not documented in the kit.
The brief said to build the plan first and build only that; the plan's api_group change could not be built, so the policy would flag every endpoint until someone resolves the syntax.
wished_for: A worked XanoScript example of a middleware file and of attaching middleware to an api_group and to a single endpoint
A rate-limit template or recipe (bot protection) so this is not a custom policy
A way to read the client IP in middleware, documented

why_confidence: The limiter middleware and table pass dry run, and the policy parses, but no endpoint attaches the middleware, so the policy would flag all endpoints and nothing is rate limited until the api_group attachment is made. The limiter itself is unverified against real traffic and its client key is spoofable.
